prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Trade, Trade versus Art, Brain, Brain versus Heart; Oh, the earthiness of these hard-hearted times, When clinking dollars, and jingling dimes, Drown all the finer music of the soul. Life as an Octopus with but this creed, That all the world was made to serve his greed; Trade has spread out his mighty myriad claw, And drawn into his foul polluted maw, The brightest and the best, Well nigh, Has he drained dry, The sacred fount of Truth; And if, forsooth, He has left yet some struggling streams from it to go, He has contaminated so their flow, That Truth, scarce is it true. Poor Art with struggling gasp, Lies strangled, dying in his mighty grasp; He locks his grimy fingers ’bout her snowy throat so tender. Is there no power to rescue her, protect, defend her? Shall Art be left to perish? Shall all the images her shrines cherish Be left to this iconoclast, to vulgar Trade? Oh, that mankind had less of Brain and more of Heart, Oh, that the world had less of Trade and more of Art; Then would there be less grinding down the poor, Then would men learn to love each other more; For Trade stalks like a giant through the land, Bearing aloft the rich in his high hand, While down beneath his mighty ponderous tread, He crushes those who cry for daily bread.

Here are two ways to polish your text depending on the format you prefer. Both options preserve all original ideas, imagery (the octopus, the giant, the strangled figure of Art, the polluted fountain of Truth), and thematic contrasts (Trade vs. Art, Brain vs. Heart, Rich vs. Poor).

---

### Option 1: Eloquent Rhetorical Prose (Best for speeches, essays, or formal prose)

> Trade versus Art, Intellect versus the Heart—how stark is the cold materialism of this unfeeling age, where the clink of coin and the jingle of silver drown out the sublime music of the human soul. 
>
> Commerce reigns like a monstrous octopus, bound to a single creed: that the world exists solely to feed its insatiable greed. Reaching out its vast, relentless tendrils, it drags the brightest and the best into its polluted maw. It has all but drained dry the sacred fountain of Truth; even the few remaining streams allowed to flow are so deeply corrupted that Truth itself is scarcely recognizable. 
>
> Meanwhile, helpless Art lies gasping, dying in its merciless grip, as grimy fingers tighten around her fair, delicate throat. Is there no power to rescue and defend her? Shall Art be left to perish? Shall the sacred treasures of her shrines be surrendered to the vulgar iconoclast of Trade? 
>
> Oh, that humanity possessed less calculating intellect and more compassion; that the world sought less of Commerce and more of Art! Only then would the oppression of the destitute cease, and humankind learn to love one another. For Trade strides like a colossus across the land—bearing the wealthy aloft in its high hand, while beneath its crushing, ponderous tread, it tramples those who cry out for their daily bread.

---

### Option 2: Polished Dramatic Verse (Best for retaining the poetic rhythm)

> Trade against Art, the Mind against the Heart—  
> Oh, the cold nature of this callous age,  
> Where clinking silver and the toll of coin  
> Drown out the soul’s most delicate refrain.  
> 
> Like an octopus driven by singular greed,  
> Believing all the world was made to serve it,  
> Trade spreads its vast and relentless claws,  
> Dragging the brightest and best into its polluted maw.  
> It has well-nigh drained the sacred fount of Truth,  
> And what struggling streams remain to flow  
> Are so tainted that Truth is scarcely true.  
> 
> Poor Art lies gasping, strangled in its grasp,  
> As grimy fingers choke her tender, fair throat.  
> Is there no power to rescue and defend her?  
> Shall Art be left to perish,  
> And the sacred treasures of her shrines  
> Be surrendered to this vulgar iconoclast?  
> 
> Would that mankind had less of Brain and more of Heart,  
> Less devoted to Trade, and more enraptured by Art!  
> Then would the grinding down of the poor diminish,  
> And humanity learn to love one another.  
> For Trade strides like a giant through the land,  
> Elevating the rich within his high hand,  
> While beneath his crushing, ponderous step,  
> He tramples those who cry for daily bread.

---

### Key Improvements Made:
* **Elevated Vocabulary:** Refined archaic or clunky phrasing (e.g., *forsooth*, *well nigh*, *earthiness*) into sophisticated, impactful language (*unfeeling age*, *callous*, *all but drained*, *destitute*).
* **Enhanced Imagery:** Smoothed out the metaphors of the **Octopus**, the **Fountain of Truth**, the **Dying Maiden (Art)**, and the **Crushing Giant** to heighten their emotional and dramatic impact.
* **Improved Rhythm & Flow:** Structured the pacing so that the contrast between industrial greed and artistic soulfulness lands with powerful rhetorical force.

In this unfeeling age, cold calculation stands opposed to empathy, just as commercial enterprise battles creative expression. The constant noise of circulating currency completely deafens us to the deeper, spiritual melodies of the human spirit. 

Mercantile greed functions like a massive octopus governed by a single principle: that the entire planet was created merely to feed its insatiable appetite. It has nearly emptied the holy spring of ultimate truth; even the few trickles that manage to escape are so deeply poisoned that honesty itself becomes questionable. 

Concurrently, artistic beauty lies choking and near death, trapped in the creature's immense grip as its dirty fingers clench around her delicate, fair neck. **The Price of Progress: Reclaiming the Soul in an Age of Commerce**

In the contemporary era, humanity finds itself defined not by its artistic achievements, moral depth, or spiritual wisdom, but by its capacity to produce and consume. Modern society is increasingly dominated by a relentless tide of commercialism and materialism—a shift in values that quietly suppresses the finer, transcendent qualities of the human soul. As the pursuit of physical wealth becomes the ultimate goal of civilization, the quieter voices of contemplation, reverence, and spiritual connection are drowned out by the noise of the marketplace.

This dominant ethos of transactionalism has had devastating consequences on the moral foundation of society. The overwhelming greed inherent in modern trade has corrupted and drained the fundamental purity of truth. Where truth was once regarded as an absolute standard to be honored and sought after, it is now routinely distorted, packaged, and manipulated to serve economic interests. Marketing tactics, corporate rhetoric, and profit-driven narratives have reduced reality itself to a commodity, sacrificing honesty on the altar of quarterly gains.

Equally tragic is the quiet death of creative expression. Art, which once served as a mirror to the human condition and a portal to the divine, is being choked to death by the vulgar and unyielding advance of commercial interests. In a world governed by profit margins, artistic endeavors are judged not by their depth, beauty, or ability to evoke profound emotion, but by their marketability and mass appeal. When creativity is forced to bow to algorithmic trends and commercial viability, it loses its revolutionary spirit and is reduced to mere entertainment.

Beyond its cultural and spiritual erosion, unchecked commercialism inflicts a devastating physical toll on human lives. Rather than creating a balanced society, modern trade operates as a mechanism that aggressively enriches a small, wealthy elite while brutally oppressing and crushing the impoverished masses. Millions of people are trapped in a relentless struggle for basic survival, their labor exploited to sustain a system that prioritizes corporate accumulation over human dignity. The gap between those who hoard wealth and those who lack basic necessities widens, exposing the profound cruelty embedded in an unregulated market.

To rescue humanity from this spiritual and social decay, a fundamental shift in priorities is urgently required. We must transcend the hyper-rational, profit-obsessed mindset that currently governs global affairs. By prioritizing heart and art over cold intellect and trade, society could begin to heal its deep wounds. Embracing artistic creation, emotional depth, and moral integrity as primary values would foster a world grounded in empathy, love, and compassion. Only by reclaiming these intrinsic human qualities can we move away from a culture of exploitation and build a society that truly honors the human spirit.
outputs.L4:
**The Leviathan of Commerce: Art, Empathy, and the Tyranny of Greed**

In the modern landscape, commercial trade no longer exists merely as a mechanism for the exchange of goods; it has morphed into a monolithic, living entity—a leviathan slithering through the heart of human culture. This monstrous figure of unchecked commerce coils its cold, metallic length around every facet of existence, tightening its grip until society gasps for air. It is a creature born of relentless ambition and fed on the altar of perpetual growth, transforming human relationships, divine truths, and creative passions into mere commodities to be bought, sold, and discarded.

At the core of this beast’s power lies a tragic shift in human values: the total surrender of empathy to cold, calculating intellect. Where heart and conscience once guided the human journey, a clinical rationale now reigns supreme. In this brave new world, truth is distorted to fit market trends, and genuine emotion is viewed as an inefficiency—a flaw in the machine. The subtle nuances of human connection are flattened into metrics, consumer demographics, and profit margins. As cold intellect displaces warmth, the capacity for true compassion blinks out, replaced by a ruthless pragmatism that measures a person’s worth solely by their productivity and purchasing power.

This systemic obsession with financial gain creates a devastating socioeconomic divide. The monster of trade is insatiable, yet its feeding habits are selectively destructive. It gorges itself on the labor of the disenfranchised, wringing the sweat and life force from the impoverished to build monuments of affluence for a select few. As the wealthy line their pockets with gold pulled from the desperate, the poor are crushed beneath the weight of an economic system designed to keep them submerged. The monster does not care for the suffering of those it tramples; it demands endless sacrifice to sustain the illusion of infinite prosperity.

Perhaps the most tragic casualty of this rampant commercialism is the human soul itself, expressed through the arts. Creativity, which once served as a sanctuary for truth and a mirror to the divine, is now violently suffocated. Poetry, painting, music, and philosophy are choked out by the heavy hand of monetization. When the arts are forced to prove their value in dollars rather than meaning, genuine expression dies. What remains is a hollow, mass-produced mimicry of culture—sanitized and packaged to ensure maximum consumption while stripping away the transformative power of true imagination.

To surrender entirely to this beast is to forfeit our humanity. The strangulation of the arts and the exploitation of the vulnerable are not inevitable consequences of human progress, but symptoms of a profound spiritual sickness. If we are to break free from the suffocating coils of commercialism, we must fundamentally realign our priorities. Society must rise to dismantle the golden idols of relentless financial gain, reclaiming a world where creative expression is nurtured, truth is cherished, and compassion is held as the highest measure of human achievement. Only by choosing empathy over profit can we sever the monster’s grip and allow the human spirit to breathe once more.
outputs.L5:
### The Mind’s Silk Road: How Art, Trade, and the Brain Shape Human Culture

At first glance, **art**, **trade**, and the human **brain** might seem like three distinct realms: one belonging to the realm of beauty and emotion, another to the cold logistics of commerce, and the third to the biological machinery of thought. Yet, throughout human history, these three forces have existed in a profound, symbiotic feedback loop. Together, they form the engine that drives cultural evolution, economic value, and the expansion of human consciousness.

#### The Creative Spark: Art and the Brain

The relationship between the brain and art is rooted in neuroaesthetics—the study of how the brain responds to visual, auditory, and experiential beauty. When we look at a painting or listen to a symphony, complex networks in the brain ignite. The visual cortex decodes shapes and colors, the limbic system surges with emotion, and the brain’s reward centers release dopamine. 

Art is not merely a passive hobby; it is a complex cognitive workout. It requires the brain to translate abstract emotions and fleeting ideas into physical form. In turn, consuming art triggers neuroplasticity, stretching the viewer's capacity for empathy, pattern recognition, and novel thinking. Art is, essentially, the externalized landscape of the human mind.

#### Assigning Value: The Neuroeconomics of Trade

While the brain generates art, it also governs the mechanism of **trade**. Trade requires a sophisticated level of abstract reasoning that is unique to humans. To exchange a basket of grain for a carved ivory figurine, the brain must perform a complex calculation: it must assign subjective value to an object based on emotional resonance, scarcity, and social status.

This intersection is where neuroeconomics takes center stage. The brain’s prefrontal cortex weighs the risk and reward of a transaction, while the amygdala responds to the desire for ownership. In the realm of high art, a piece of painted canvas can be worth millions of dollars simply because collective human brains agree upon its symbolic value. Trade is not just an exchange of goods; it is an exchange of perceived mental value.

#### The Global Circuitry: How Trade Spreads Art and Reshapes Minds

If the brain creates art, trade is the network that distributes it. Historically, trade routes like the Silk Road were far more than commercial highways for silk and spices; they were the superhighways of cultural exchange. 

When merchants traded physical objects, they also traded aesthetic ideas. Renaissance Italy’s artistic explosion was fueled by trade with the Byzantine and Islamic worlds, which brought new pigments (like ultramarine derived from lapis lazuli), techniques, and mathematical perspectives. Centuries later, the trade of Japanese woodblock prints to Europe radically rewired the brains of Impressionist painters like Claude Monet and Vincent van Gogh, altering how they perceived light and space.

When trade introduces new forms of art to a culture, it literally changes how the brains of that population process the world. New visual motifs, musical scales, and storytelling structures create new neural pathways, inspiring fresh bursts of creativity.

#### Conclusion: The Engine of Human Progress

The story of civilization is written at the crossroads of the brain, art, and trade. The **brain** imagines the impossible; **art** gives that imagination a tangible form; and **trade** carries that creation across geographic and cultural divides, exposing new brains to new ideas. 

In our modern digital era, this loop moves faster than ever. Digital trade networks instantly transport visual art, music, and ideas across the globe, continuing to reshape the global brain. As long as humans possess the neurological capacity to create and the desire to connect, art and trade will remain the twin sails driving the human mind forward.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a 19th-century style poem about how commercial greed and trade are destroying art and human compassion.
counterfactuals.output:
**The Gilded Chain**

Where once the Muse attuned her golden lyre,
And gentle Pity wept for human woe,
Now burns the altar of a colder fire,
Where streams of trade and selfish lucre flow.
The ancient woods are felled for iron beams,
The skies are darkened by the factory's breath;
And in the rush of avaricious schemes,
The quiet soul is trampled unto death.

No sacred work escapes the merchant’s eye,
No grace remains untouched by vulgar trade;
The poet’s song, that soared into the sky,
Is measured now by how a price is made.
The canvas, once a window to the soul,
Where divine beauty cast a holy light,
Is bought and hoarded like a miser's dole,
To hide in vaults, secluded from the sight.

Alas for Pity! In the bustling mart,
Where every groan is weighed against a coin,
No brother’s pain can move the hardened heart,
Nor simple grief two human spirits join.
With ledger-books for bibles, men rehearse
The cold arithmetic of gain and loss,
And sell their freedom for a heavier purse,
Exchanging Heaven for a gilded dross.

The loom hums loud to weave a shroud of gold,
While mercy starves outside the counting-door;
The warmth of love grows measurably cold,
And rich men flourish as the soul grows poor.
O Iron Age! Thou hast dethroned the Sun,
And set a penny where the heart should beat;
Thy triumphs end where virtue is undone,
And beauty lies polluted in the street.

The song is hushed; the marble turned to dust;
The gentle impulse slain by selfish gain.
We trade our birthright for a fleeting lust,
And call us masters in a gilded chain.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you write a dramatic Victorian poem contrasting "Trade versus Art" and "Brain versus Heart"? Use imagery like Trade as a greedy octopus strangling Art and a giant crushing the poor underfoot.
counterfactuals.output:
Upon the soot-stained cobblestones of Time,
Where Mammon builds his towering iron throne,
We sell the sacred, elevate the crime,
And turn the living spirit into stone.
Two mighty forces battle in the dark,
To claim the throne where human destinies start:
The cold, computing Brain against the Spark,
The titan Trade against the weeping Heart.

The Great Cold Brain computes the worth of tears
In ledgers bound in dark, relentless red;
It weighs a lifetime not by love, but years,
And counts the profit where the passion bled.
It knows no mercy, worships only Scheme,
It measures music by the cost of thread;
It dissects grace to starve the poet’s dream,
And offers stone to those who beg for bread.

Behold great Trade! An octopus of greed,
Whose writhing tendrils stretch o’er sea and land!
It grips the canvas for its insatiate need,
And snaps the lyre within the painter's hand.
Its slimy suckers coil around the throat
Of gentle Art, who gasps for holy air;
It chokes her song, her sweet, celestial note,
And leaves her pale, strangled in despair.

And lo! High-towering o'er the smoky town,
An iron Giant strides through alleyways!
With boots of brass he treads the wretched down,
And shortens poor men’s miserable days.
He crushes weeping mothers in the mire,
He steps on starving children as they cry;
He feeds their broken bones into his fire,
To paint a golden ruin on the sky.

Oh, wretched age! Where Brain hath slain the Soul,
And ledger-lines replace the altar’s grace!
Where Trade’s dark engine claims the ultimate toll,
And sweeps divine creation from the place!
What boots the gold that fills the merchant's vault,
If every song is hushed, and color dead?
If human mercy fails by cold default,
And art lies murdered in a copper bed?

For Brain without a Heart is but a shroud,
A mechanical horror, cold and bleak;
And Trade without an Art is but a cloud
That blinds the strong and smothers out the weak.
Woe to the world that sells its soul for gain,
Where giants tread and monstrous hydras reign!
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem lamenting how modern materialism and the pursuit of money drown out the music of the soul, truth, and artistic expression.
counterfactuals.output:
Once, every chest held sacred, silent chords,
An inner song of timber, breath, and light.
Now drowned beneath the chatter of our lords,
The clinking coins that echo through the night.

We built high temples out of glass and gold,
And traded canvas for the ledger’s line;
The ancient truths were auctioned off and sold
To buy the empty glitter of the mine.

The poet’s pen is trimmed to fit the trade,
The singer sells her sorrow by the page,
And art, once born where holy shadows played,
Now dances, chained, upon a neon stage.

No longer do we listen to the wind,
Nor heed the quiet music of the soul;
Through cold, relentless thirst we all have sinned,
And shattered what was beautifully whole.

We buy the world, yet perish in the drought,
Our pockets heavy, but our spirits bare;
The harp of truth is choked and rusted out,
And only cold arithmetic fills the air.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a passionate rhyming poem critiquing commercialism, written in the tone of a Gilded Age social critic.
counterfactuals.output:
Behold the age of filigree and glass,  
Where gilded pride obscures the rotting brass!  
The street is paved with promises of gold,  
Yet every sacred thing is bought and sold.  
Upon the altar of the marketplace,  
We strip the beauty from the human race;  
We trade the immortal spirit for a fee,  
And call this shameful auction *Liberty*.  

The peddler cries his false and glittered wares,  
While Mammon sits above our frantic prayers.  
From velvet parlors to the tenement,  
In cold transaction all our days are spent.  
No mountain peak escapes the sign-board’s art,  
No quiet grove is safe from commerce’ dart;  
They weigh the air, they price the morning breeze,  
And hang a toll on God’s eternal trees!  

Oh, see the Captains of this hollow State,  
Who measure virtue by the freight-train’s rate!  
They build their towers high on sunken bones,  
And swap the heart’s true wealth for precious stones.  
The crowd pursues the bauble for its shine,  
And drinks the dross, mistaking it for wine—  
A nation chained to ledger-lines and gain,  
Where love is coin, and honor but a stain.  

What worth the damask or the marble floor,  
When starving spirits rattle at the door?  
You buy the canvas, yet you blind the eye;  
You claim the earth, but cannot own the sky.  
The loom spins fast, the iron engine groans,  
To grind our living flesh to factory stones,  
While fat apostles of the Ticker-Tape  
Proclaim that Progress wears a golden shape.  

Repent, ye merchant-kings of grand deceit!  
The rust shall eat your vault and judgment seat.  
For when the final balance sheet is drawn,  
And night descends upon your gilded dawn,  
Your mounds of bullion cannot buy the breath  
To bribe the dark, inevitable Death.  
Awake, O mankind! Break the market gate,  
Reclaim your soul before it is too late!
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem about a monstrous entity named Trade who chokes out Art with grimy fingers and crushes those begging for daily bread, ending with a plea for more heart and less trade in the world.
counterfactuals.output:
Upon the earth a titan stands,
With iron heart and soot-stained hands.
His name is Trade, a beast of greed,
Who feeds upon our human need.
His eyes are coins of heavy brass,
He treads, and all the flowers pass.

With grimy fingers, rough and cold,
He grabs at Art to turn to gold.
He coils around her slender throat,
And smothers every golden note.
Her spirit gasps, her colors fade
Beneath the callous grip of Trade;
He snaps her brush, he breaks her lyre,
And quenches her celestial fire.

Beneath his cruel and grinding heel,
The desperate cry, the hungry kneel.
For those who beg for daily bread
Are crushed beneath his heavy tread.
They raise their thin and hollow palms,
Receiving blows instead of alms,
While Trade demands his pound of rust
And grinds their bones into the dust.

Oh, world of ledgers, dark and bleak,
Where profit silences the weak,
Must all of beauty be erased
To keep this monster well-embraced?

Hear now the plea from every street,
Where soul and sorrow bitter meet:
Unclench the fist, tear down the mart,
Let beauty breathe, let passion start.
Oh, heal the world in every part—
Give us less Trade, and give more Heart.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
